claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a disordered single-phase BCC solid solution.
The equiatomic alloy has high configurational entropy.
Atomic-size mismatch in the random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution produces significant lattice distortion.
Thermal annealing or controlled cooling can induce short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
The induced short-range order preferentially forms HfTi and TiZr B2-like binary clusters.
HfTi and TiZr B2-like clusters can nucleate and percolate while the alloy retains a single-phase BCC matrix.
Short-range ordering can be activated below the order-disorder transition temperature of the corresponding bulk intermetallics.
B2-like ordering reduces the variance in atomic-size mismatch within the clusters relative to a random atomic distribution.
The ordered clusters locally relax the lattice strain field and reduce effective lattice-distortion amplitude.
Reduced local lattice distortion decreases the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
A percolating network of ordered clusters creates low-resistance pathways for phonon transport.
Above the cluster percolation threshold, reduced phonon scattering and percolative transport produce a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random alloy.
Ordering shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS peak to higher frequencies because of stiffer local bonds.
Ordering increases the group velocities associated with the high-frequency phonon DOS.
Mean-square atomic displacement within the ordered clusters is lower than in the random alloy.
The random HfNbTaTiZr alloy has ultra-low lattice thermal conductivity because lattice distortion strongly scatters phonons.
Below the cluster percolation threshold, isolated ordered clusters increase scattering and reduce conductivity.
Long-range phase separation or precipitation of secondary phases such as sigma phase reintroduces strong phonon scattering and bounds the conductivity increase.
The percolation threshold for short-range-ordered clusters in HfNbTaTiZr is currently unknown.
